intervention.sample: start of round 8 for each surviving seat on each independent map
intervention.baseline: frozen routed-v6 direct policy for the entire continuation
intervention.candidate: reply-search 256 root nodes, eight completed-turn candidates, 64 reply nodes for one whole turn, then the same frozen direct policy
intervention.outcome: exact terminal result or the configured action-limit adjudication; censoring reported separately

interpretation: The complete reply-search agent has a validated full-game advantage over routed-v6 on separate fresh maps, but substituting only one searched whole turn and then reverting to routed-v6 does not show a positive conditional outcome effect. The labels are sparse and sometimes negative; this does not prove that any individual searched move is intrinsically bad or that reply-search is weak. It does show why treating every search action as an equally beneficial supervised target is unjustified. Future distillation should use sustained trajectories or outcome-grounded policy optimization, with fresh complete-game gates.
